STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole citrus fruit (orange or mandarin) on a white square plate, photographed from directly overhead. A few small orange peel bits and juice smears are on the plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square plate is about 24 cm across its diagonal-ish longest width, roughly 22 cm per side. The plate is about 260 px wide in the image along its side, so the scale is roughly 0.085 cm/px. Plate area is about 22 x 22 = ~480 cm² (a bit less due to rounded corners, ~450 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items: one whole orange/mandarin; tiny peel fragments (negligible).

STEP 4 - Area: The fruit is about 122 px across, which is about 10 cm if the scale is 0.085 cm/px. Hmm, that suggests a large fruit. Check against the plate: the plate side is about 330 px, so if it is 22 cm, the scale is 0.067 cm/px and the fruit is about 8 cm across. That is plausible for an orange. The fruit area is 3.14 x 4² = ~50 cm², or about 11% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: A sphere with an 8 cm diameter has a volume of about 268 ml. The fruit looks slightly squat, so about 250 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit density is about 0.9 g/ml, giving about 225 g. Peel and fruit together weigh about this much, so I'll say about 200 g (allowing for a slightly smaller fruit).

STEP 7 - Energy: Orange is about 47 kcal/100 g, so 200 g is about 94 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A large orange weighs about 180-230 g with peel and has about 85-100 kcal. This is consistent.
